checks.comparison: Difference initialization dispatches one same-component (x,y) difference per worker for positive S, with zero initial count/sum. Every matching nondecreasing-clock reply increments count once, adds its value and immediately assigns a fresh component to that worker, including the S-th accepted reply. Further updates freeze once count>=target. DifferenceResult divides by the fixed target S. Thus the literal final unused dispatch is represented while later PAGE control must stop waiting at S; completed IID and cost bounds are not asserted here.

Full initialization retains the original label list and distinct occurrence IDs0..q-1, dispatches one selected label per worker using distinct offset rows/IDs, and starts the sum at zero. A matching nondecreasing-clock completion removes one still-needed occurrence of its component and adds the reply only if such an occurrence exists; otherwise it discards the obsolete value. The finishing worker is immediately reassigned from the remaining occurrence list, or receives None when empty. FullResult divides the accumulated raw sum by the fixed original cardinality. Post-empty updates freeze. This preserves multiset multiplicities and the reviewed empty-final-sample guard; the scalar-distribution equality with source incremental normalization remains part of correctness proof.

All definitions preserve natural dimensions, worker counts, finite label lists and finite NNReal clocks. Multiset cardinality may exceed m; zero-size invalid states remain total. No positive-duration, finite-tau, finite-expectation or distinct-component restriction is added.

The original list fixes the full denominator and occurrence-label map; difference x/y and target remain constant. Replies match the current pending worker ID before update. Initial IDs are firstID+i and nextID starts at firstID+n; subsequent dispatches use and increment nextID. Global cross-batch uniqueness still requires the caller to propagate the offset.

These are complete state and transition definitions, without assumed invariants, IID, accuracy or time conclusions. Invalid/idle/unmatched/backward-clock replies leave state unchanged. Correct reply values and legal active requests come from the reviewed primitive oracle contract plus later execution invariants. No informal collector-proof preparation is used as proof evidence here. The source contains complete definitions only; future registered collector correctness and timing theorems must still be proved.

No new hypothesis or public admissibility predicate is introduced. Source fixed points, multiset labels and target S are data; actual exact-gradient behavior, fresh row usage, conditional schedule independence and finite-event progress are proved or supplied by their separate reviewed providers.

The full result uses the original cardinality and the difference result uses target S. Raw sums are scaled only at result extraction, algebraically matching source incremental divisions in exact real vector arithmetic. Fixed points and the (x,y) difference orientation match the source.

The concrete transitions implement source initial parallel dispatch, matching-completion processing, obsolete full-value discard and immediate reassignment. Full completion avoids sampling an empty set; difference completion retains the S-th unused reassignment. Stops are state guards, with the surrounding PAGE controller responsible for ending queries/resetting the batch. Current source inspection confirms that fullUpdate searches for one remaining occurrence of the completed component, preserving multiplicity even when several occurrence IDs carry that label. DifferenceUpdate performs the final replacement before the subsequent done guard freezes state.

Private row functions are passed as data, never replaced by oracle-controlled samples. Initial workers use distinct offset coordinates, later dispatches advance nextID, and occurrence selection uses the accepted row law. These definitions do not claim conditional IID; adaptive counter freshness and completed-label independence remain later proofs.

Both collector nodes are algorithmic supporting definitions. No convergence wrapper, success predicate, budget or time theorem is asserted. Required correctness/event-count/runtime propositions remain in their separately planned proof units.

A list of occurrence IDs with a fixed original label array preserves arbitrary multiset multiplicities. One Option job per worker implements pending work; finite clock and explicit IDs support cancellation/matching. Generic selectedLabel is a concrete implementation helper, not an extra source claim.

The module directly imports Template and the accepted FreyaRandomness dependency closure. It uses the reviewed model job/query/reply types and private selection functions; no hidden source theorem or independent-completion conclusion is imported or assumed.

Native format/style/declaration and topology gates passed before review. The two algorithm nodes retain their intended initial/update/result mappings. Generated record/matcher declarations and the selectedLabel helper are reviewed as implementation structure, with no extra public catalog entry. The current source, unit, dependency inventory and gate observations were identity-checked against prior independent analysis. The global plan difference consists only of later conditional_costs helper names, with no effect on these transitions.

Empty full input produces no pending jobs and freezes; S=0 produces no difference jobs and freezes. m=0/n=0 remain type-correct invalid cases. Equal completion clocks are accepted, so zero-duration simultaneous events are permitted. Duplicate labels delete one occurrence per useful reply. Late unmatched IDs and decreasing clocks are rejected.
